text.p: These are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Negotiating with industrial trade unions, government agrees to raise 1997 profit tax rate by 10 percent. Workers expect their net salaries to grow by same percentage.
- Government drafts law to become owner of significant assets formerly owned by communist party and similar institutions. Assets should then go to various political parties.
- Parliament discusses new law on flat renting which would finally cancel institution of social ownership.
- First and second instalment of loans extended to hoteliers last spring to be paid from state budget. Further payments will come from hoteliers, but not earlier than next summer.
- New law on real estate ownership proposes long-term loans payable within 30 years with five to six percent annual interest rates, giving preference to young couples and families with more children.
- Three years of monetary stability. National Bank's governor Marko Skreb says average annual inflation is one percent.
- United opposition asks parliament to change laws to solve long crisis over Zagreb mayoralty. If this fails new measures of pressure against ruling HDZ party will follow.
- It is too soon to talk of Croatian economic miracle when country still in a period of "dynamic recovery", says Stjepan Zdunic of the Economic Institute. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
